title: Wear on Quay Street: stains, grime, gum, cracked render and the street's other marks
summary_line: 33 kinds of seeded greyscale wear mask, each with its rule of place, size and shape in metres, density, tone per surface, wet and dry look, texel scale and checks, from 29 measurements on CC0 photographs and the Hook sheet; facade-wide soot (two houses of thirteen, grey) and the dark head (under gable verges, not eaves gutters) are kinds of their own, streaks follow the photographs, wet and dry are kept apart, and nothing from 2000s Britain or America is in it.

units.tone: sRGB 0-255, albedo multiplier in linear light, L* is CIE D65

scene.street: Quay Street, the Hook, Meridian; 48 m, 6.0 m carriageway (two 3.0 m lanes, crossfall 1:40, crown 75 mm above the channel), footways 2.0 m (1:40), kerb upstand 0.125, channel course 0.255 wide
scene.east_side: six-bay Victorian shop parade, 6 m bays, faces WEST (the wet side in the UK's prevailing south-westerly)
scene.west_side: shop block (north half) and plain terraces (quay end), faces EAST

streak_sill.label: Rain streaks under window sills

where.feature: the lower edge of a window sill, upper floors and shop transom ledges alike; a set under 15 to 60 % of sills (typical 35 %), never under every sill
where.rule: Origin on the sill's lower edge. A set holds two end streaks under the sill's two ends, which differ in length (longer over shorter 1.15 to 2.5) and in width (wider over narrower at least 1.1); 3 to 7 thin rivulets from brackets, joints and chips along the sill; and a faint wash. One set in 8 has a long end streak of 0.8 to 1.4 m (a sill with a broken drip). Everything runs straight down, tilted at most 3 degrees. Never rotate a streak. The continuous darkening under a gutter, verge or coping is wall_head_band, not this kind.
where.height_m: 0 to 0.6 below the sill's lower edge (0.8 to 1.4 for a long end streak); stop at the next ledge, string course or door head if nearer
where.sides: East parade fronts face west, the wet side of a British port: weight 1.0. West block fronts face east: weight 0.7. Gable ends facing the street: 0.8.
where.footfall_and_wet: Not footfall. Wet climate: always present; darker and glossier when wet; the lower half dries first.

density.unit: share of sills that carry a set
density.src: Photo M23: of about 30 sill and ledge edges counted by eye in five views of urban_street_03, one carries a clear streak (M17); a column test on 13 edges finds one darker than 0.90 under 2 and none darker than 0.85 (3 to 15 %). That street is maintained 2019 brick, the cleanest end of the range (S2), so the target raises it for an uncleaned 1990 street and Jafar's 'not faint marks' of 2 October: Judgement. The reviewer's 50 to 70 % is not measured anywhere and is kept as the upper bound (D6)

streak_coping.label: Fingers under leaking joints in copings, ledges, string courses and gutters

wall_foot_splash.label: Pavement splash and grime band on walls, stallrisers and door bottoms
wall_foot_splash.layer: L0 in the material (height gradient) plus L1 decal for the ragged top edge

where.feature: the foot of every wall that meets the pavement: brick walls, stallrisers, pilaster plinths, door leaves' bottom rails, door steps
where.rule: A band from the pavement upward. Full strength from 0 to 0.24 m, 0.85 at 0.33 m, 0.45 at 0.49 m, 0.15 at 0.61 m, gone by 0.75 m; the top edge is ragged and steps in brick-course heights (75 mm) on brick, in small blotches on painted timber. Within 0.6 m of a door or a downpipe the band is 1.2 x higher and 1.15 x stronger (strength capped at 1). It REPLACES the foot rise of the recipe's wear layer (section 1) and is multiplied after wall_soot and wall_foot_damp (section 4).
where.height_m: 0 to 0.75 above the pavement (the Hook sheet gable: black to 0.33 m, half gone at 0.49 m); x 1.2 within 0.6 m of a door or downpipe
where.sides: Both sides; heavier on the east parade where the pavement is wetter (north-facing step shadow not modelled)
where.footfall_and_wet: Footfall and wet: strongest at shop doors and the quay-end corner where people stand; splash is wet-pavement spatter from boots and rain bounce.

It is multiplied BEFORE wall_foot_splash (section 4), so the foot is damp x splash, and only above 0.75 m is it alone. where.rule: Strength by state: sooted 1.0, as built 0.35, cleaned 0.0 (Judgement; the sheet's walls read as built or cleaned). Which houses are sooted is decided from the sheet (D13): the sheet's frame shows no house darker than about 0.86 of Mickey's front, so no parade bay and no west_south bay is sooted; sooted houses are the chandler and west_north bay 2 (2 of 13). At strength 1 the albedo multiplier is 0.42 (Photo M21: 0.377, 0.37 to 0.48). THE SOOT KEEPS LITTLE OF THE BRICK'S COLOUR: soot is a nearly neutral deposit (M21 92/81/73), not a red filter. The mark on brick_red is the review's 82/62/55 (L* 28.2, C* 10.8: 0.39 of the clean brick's chroma 27.6), a lerp toward M21's soot, stored as 81/61/54 so that its luminance is exactly x 0.42 of the brick's; brick_painted and render_cream likewise (the same luminance multiplier, their own hue, chroma x 0.39). Target: the composed sooted wall keeps 0.4 to 0.6 of the clean wall's CIE chroma (Photo M21 0.43 to 0.54, Sheet head 0.39 to 0.42). The mask is a metre-scale mottle (wavelength 0.5 to 2.0 m, std 0.07) around a mean level 0.90, plus the darker lower wall: the level rises by 0.10 below 0.7 m and is back to the body by 1.2 m, which is x 0.88 on the wall above (Sheet M22: lower wall about x 0.90 over 0.17 to 0.77 m up on the right-hand cottage; check lower_wall_excess). The mask is for the whole wall including above 4 m (the builder repeats the 4 m row).

where.sides: Both sides; the state, not the side, decides: sooted 2 of 13 houses (the chandler, west_north bay 2), as built 9, cleaned 2 (target.json `houses`)

where.feature: the lower edge of a gable verge or barge (full strength), of a chimney-stack or parapet coping and a string course (the coping scale), and, at 0 to 0.2 of the strength and 0.1 to 0.3 m deep, of the eaves gutter of a front
where.rule: Sheet M22 measures the left gable under its VERGE: a verge with no gutter, where roof water runs straight down the brick. The sheet shows no such head under an eaves gutter (Mickey's front, M28: 0.64 of the body in the first 10 rows, the dentil course's shadow, then 0.85 to 1.18 by band, mean 1.0; the review 1.00 to 1.10, down to 0.5 m) and none under the right-hand cottage's gable verge (flat, 0.036 to 0.063, columns 1560 to 1595, rows 322 to 478), so the head is a weighted rule, not a rule for every roof edge. Gable verge or barge: multiplier at mask 1 0.56 on a wall that is as built or cleaned (Sheet M22, wet 0.50 to 0.62 over the top 0.2 to 0.75 m, divided by the wet 0.90) and 0.80 on a sooted wall (Photo M21: a further x 0.80 under the coping of the sooted panel; nothing is darkened twice); weight 1.0 on the quay-facing gables (the sheet's left gable: Mickey's quay gable and west_south's, x 3) and 0.3 to 1.0 by house seed on other gables. Depth profile by distance below the feature: 1.0 to 0.2 m, 0.85 at 0.4 m, 0.70 at 0.6 m, 0.30 at 0.75 m, 0.18 at 0.95 m, 0 by 1.15 m (Sheet M22: 0.75 to 0.80 at 0.9 to 1.0 m, 1.0 by 1.4 m wet). Parapet and chimney copings and string courses keep the coping scale: the same profile x 0.3 in depth (Photo M21: a band 0.4 m deep), weight 1.0. Eaves gutter of a front: strength 0 to 0.2 and depth 0.1 to 0.3 m, the depth being where the profile reaches half strength (the profile compressed by depth / 0.675; Judgement, from Mickey's front); a leaking gutter is streak_coping's job. The lower edge is ragged by whole brick courses: the profile slides up or down by 75 mm steps (its standard deviation along x 20 to 100 mm), so the edge always lies on a course line. It REPLACES the recipe's head water paths (STREAK_DEPTH, section 1).

The patch colour is a pale ochre, 141/102/72 on the wet sheet's near-black paint 50/40/37 (Sheet M25), 152/110/78 dry. era_rules: Heavy: 1990 walls were sootier and 1990 pavements dirtier than any modern panorama measured (the 2019 London photographs are the cleanest end of the range, though their brick does show soot, M21). Where a photograph and the Hook sheet disagree, the sheet governs the mood of wall feet and heads (a WET street: converted to dry, section 4) and the photographs govern what the sheet does not show (streaks, M23) and the ground.

Nothing later than 1990, or unusual in an old quarter then (Judgement on each): no tactile or blister paving, red or green anti-skid surfacing, thermoplastic bus lanes, pressure-washed stripes, bike-lane green, spray utility markings, cycle stands, wheelie-bin lines, vape and mask litter, QR-code stickers, anti-bird spikes, uPVC white fronts.

No American marks: no wide white parking T-markings, no painted crosswalk zebras in white 12-inch bars, no manhole lids with US castings, no fire-hydrant paint, no yellow centre-line pairs, no graffiti throw-ups in bubble-letter style (the street's graffiti are the canon's five tags, in another family).
No alcohol or gambling traces: no bottles, cans, bar-mats, betting slips or scratch cards in the litter (canon content rule). Tobacco ends are allowed.

check_measures.coverage: share of decal pixels with mask >= thr (default 0.5)
check_measures.blob_eqd_mm: equivalent diameter (mm) = 2 sqrt(area / pi) of the 8-connected components of mask >= thr (default 0.5) with area >= min_area_mm2; stat p50 (default) or p90 over the components
check_measures.count_per_m2: number of 8-connected components of mask >= thr with area >= min_area_mm2, per m2 of the decal frame
check_measures.edge_10_90_mm: 10 to 90 % edge width, relative to the mask's own peak: 0.95 x peak / the 90th percentile of |gradient| (per metre; one axis if axis is x or y), taken over pixels with band_lo x peak < mask < band_hi x peak (defaults 0.1 and 0.9) that lie within reach_mm (default 60) of the contour at half the peak; 0 if the peak is below 0.2
check_measures.streak_aspect: median over the 8-connected components of mask >= thr (default 0.3) with rod length >= min_length_m of rod length / rod width; rod length = sqrt(12 x variance) along the major axis, width likewise along the minor axis
check_measures.streak_width_mm: stat (p50 default, p10 or p90) over those components of the rod width in mm
check_measures.streak_length_m: stat (p50 default, p10 or p90) over those components of the rod length in m
check_measures.verticality_deg: largest deviation of a component's major axis from vertical (degrees) over the components of mask >= thr (default 0.3) with rod length >= min_length_m (default 0.1 m)
check_measures.fade_ratio: per component of mask >= thr (default 0.3) taller than 150 mm: mean mask over its last third of rows / its first third; median over components
check_measures.foot_profile: mean mask per row of the whole decal width, at each point [height_m, min, max], mean of three rows: axis rows_from_bottom counts height up from the frame's bottom row (the pavement line), rows_from_top counts down from its top row (the feature's lower edge); the check passes when at least 80 % of the points are inside their bounds
check_measures.tile_seam: mean |mask(first column) - mask(last column)| (rows for axis y; the larger of the two for xy) divided by the mean absolute difference of adjacent columns (rows) inside the tile: about 1 when seamless
check_measures.top_edge_std_mm: standard deviation along x, in mm, of the far edge of the band: for each column the row farthest from the source edge (source bottom: the pavement line, the frame's bottom row; source top: the feature's lower edge, the top row) where mask >= thr; columns without such a row are left out; 0 if fewer than 60 % of the columns have one
check_measures.column_mean_cv: coefficient of variation (std / mean) across x of the column means of the mask over the rows from_m to to_m (m) measured from the source edge (source bottom or top)
check_measures.brick_patch_share: share of brick cells whose mean mask is above cell_mean_above (default 0.4): cells brick_w_m x brick_h_m in stretcher bond (courses brick_h_m high from the pavement line, each course offset by half a brick), only courses lying wholly between from_m and to_m, only whole cells inside the frame
check_measures.brick_cell_std: mean over the cells counted as whitened in brick_patch_share (same cells, same parameters) of the standard deviation of the mask inside the cell
check_measures.end_streak_length_ratio: longer over shorter rod length of the leftmost and rightmost components of mask >= thr (default 0.25) whose top lies within head_m (default 0.2) of the frame's top edge (the sill's lower edge); 0 if there are fewer than two
check_measures.end_streak_width_ratio: wider over narrower rod width of the same two end components
check_measures.rivulet_count: number of the components between those two end components, in x order, with rod length >= min_length_m (default 0.1)
check_measures.finger_spacing_cv: std / mean of the gaps between the centres of the runs of mask >= thr (default 0.25) along the row head_row_m (default 0.12 m) below the frame's top edge; 0 if fewer than three runs
check_measures.finger_length_cv: std / mean of the rod lengths of the components of mask >= thr whose top lies within head_m of the top edge; 0 if fewer than three
check_measures.nn_ratio: Clark-Evans ratio of the components of mask >= thr (area >= min_area_mm2; at least 4): mean nearest-neighbour distance of their centroids / (0.5 / sqrt(n / A)), A the frame area (area frame) or the convex hull of the centroids (area hull); about 1 for random scatter, above 1.3 for a lattice, below 0.8 for clusters; 0 if fewer than four
check_measures.size_cv: std / mean of the equivalent diameters of the components of mask >= thr with area >= min_area_mm2 (at least 4)
check_measures.dominant_wavelength_m: wavelength 1 / (k x f) in m of the annulus with the largest summed power in the 2-D power spectrum of the mask minus its mean, annuli of width f = 1 / the shorter side of the frame (m), k = 1, 2, 3, ... the annulus index (the zero-frequency annulus is left out)
check_measures.core_column_cv: coefficient of variation (std / mean) across x of the column means of the mask over the FULL-STRENGTH zone, the rows from_m to to_m (m) measured from the source edge (source bottom or top); a band in vertical stripes is refused
check_measures.edge_on_course_share: share of columns whose far edge of the band (as in top_edge_std_mm, at mask >= thr, measured from the source edge: the row farthest from it, taken as the outer boundary of that row) lies within tol_mm (default 10) of a multiple of course_m (default 0.075 m, a brick course) from the source edge; 0 if fewer than 60 % of the columns have an edge
check_measures.brick_neighbour_same_share: share of pairs of side-by-side brick cells in a course (cells as in brick_patch_share, same parameters) that are both on (cell mean above cell_mean_above) or both off; a checkerboard gives 0, a random fill of 0.55 about 0.5, a solid stripe 1
check_measures.rivulet_spacing_cv: std / mean of the gaps between the x centres of the rivulet components (the components between the two end components, rod length >= min_length_m, as for rivulet_count); 0 if there are fewer than three
check_measures.rivulet_length_cv: std / mean of the rod lengths of the same rivulet components; 0 if there are fewer than three
check_measures.lower_wall_excess: mean of the mask over the rows low_from_m to low_to_m (default 0.1 to 0.6 m) minus its mean over the rows high_from_m to high_to_m (default 1.5 to 3.5 m), heights from the bottom row (the pavement line)
check_measures.coverage_share_below_m: share of the pixels with mask >= thr (default 0.5) that lie in the lowest below_m (default 0.3 m) of the frame (its bottom rows); 0 if there are none
check_measures.tone_ratio: mean luminance of the dark-slab class over the pale-slab class in the generated flag colour map (check applies to the flag colour result, not the mask)
check_measures.crack_flag_share: share of flags carrying a crack in the generated flag attributes
check_measures.crack_width_mm: median of 2 x distance-transform - 1 along the Zhang-Suen skeleton of mask >= thr (mm)
check_measures.crack_length_per_m2: skeleton length (m) of mask >= thr per m2 of the decal frame
check_measures.role_length_per_m2: envelope polygons only (drawing check): path length of the polygons with the named role per m2 of the frame
check_measures.role_blob_eqd_mm: envelope polygons only (drawing check): equivalent diameter of the polygons with the named role (stat p50 or p90)
check_measures.role_count: envelope polygons only (drawing check): number of polygons with the named role
check_measures.role_share_below: envelope polygons only (drawing check): share (by polygon area, of=area, or by count) of the polygons with the named role whose centroid lies below below_mm of the frame's bottom edge
check_measures.house_to_house_ratio: composition: for every house of target.json `houses` that the Hook sheet's frame shows, the mean linear luminance of its composed upper wall (rows from 1.3 m up, wall_soot at the house's state weight, albedo, no haze) over Mickey's front's (east_parade_bay0); the value returned is the one furthest from 1 (so the darkest and the brightest are both tested)
check_measures.composed_soot_chroma_ratio: composition: CIE chroma (L*a*b*, D65) of the mean colour of the composed sooted wall (state sooted, rows from 1.3 m up, brick_red) over the clean brick's
check_measures.composed_eaves_front_ratio: composition: luminance over the wall's, mean over x, of a wall under its eaves gutter composed with wall_head_band at the stated strength (default 0.2) and depth_m (default 0.3: the profile compressed in depth so that its half-strength height, 0.675 m, falls at depth_m, factor depth_m / 0.675), at below_m (default 0.3 m) below the eaves
check_measures.composed_foot_ratio: composition (compose block, self_check.compose_walls; every composition measure takes either the target's own drawn envelopes or, for unit 4.5, a `masks` dict of the builder's own masks): the luminance of a composed 2 m brick foot beside a downpipe (wall_soot, wall_foot_damp, wall_foot_splash, algae_downpipe in the stated order, then the floor, at house wear 1.0, dry, in the state given) over the clean wall's, mean over x 0.6 to 1.4 m at height_m (default 0.1)
check_measures.composed_salt_ratio: composition: luminance over the clean wall's of the composed foot at the whitened bricks (salt mask > 0.4) between 0.30 and 0.52 m, after the replacing marks
check_measures.composed_wall_min_ratio: composition: the lowest luminance over the clean wall's anywhere on the composed foot before the replacing marks (the floor is working when it is not below the wall floor)
check_measures.composed_soot_ratio: composition: mean luminance of the sooted house's composed wall (soot state weight 1.0) over the cleaned house's (weight 0.0), rows from 1.3 m up
check_measures.composed_head_ratio: composition: luminance over the wall's of the composed head band at depth 0.1 m below the feature, wall_soot in the given state first, mean over x
check_measures.channel_over_road: composition: luminance of the channel_concrete albedo after the channel body's gutter_grime (mean over the channel rows 0.06 to 0.23 m) over the asphalt_dry albedo's
check_measures.fringe_over_road: composition: luminance of the asphalt_dry albedo after the gutter_grime fringe (mean over rows 0.30 to 0.45 m) over the unmarked asphalt_dry albedo's

houses.look_rule: `look_hue_only` is the recipe's look for the house (HOUSE_LOOKS picked by (brick_set + seed) % 4, bay 0 fixed at look 0, times its own value 0.78 to 1.0 and warm lean, as _house_tint computes it) divided by the luminance it gives on the brick (brick_red) wall, so only its hue is kept and wall_soot's state carries all of the brightness. compose.rule: Marks are applied to the clean albedo in a fixed order, then clamped at a floor, then the replacing marks are laid. A darkening mark (albedo_mult_linear < 1) multiplies per channel by lerp(1, ratio_c, mask x strength) with ratio_c = mark_lin_c / surface_lin_c (the dirt tint travels in the stored mark colour; linear light); a replacing mark (multiplier 1.0) is lerp(colour, mark_lin, mask x strength) over the colour already darkened. Strength = house wear (0.55 to 1.0) x the side weight x, for wall_soot, the state weight. One surface per decal: the placer picks the tone row from the material under the decal's origin and a decal that crosses two surfaces is split at the joint.

walls.floor_basis: The product of the darkening multipliers on any texel is clamped at 0.15 of the clean albedo's luminance (the colour is scaled up to it, hue kept) before the replacing marks. The Hook sheet's darkest foot is 0.12 to 0.30 of its wall (M18). Unclamped, a sooted foot beside a downpipe stacks soot 0.42 x damp 0.5 x splash 0.27 x algae 0.40 = 0.02; at house wear 1.0 on a cleaned wall, splash x damp x algae is 0.05.
walls.salt: salt_bloom is a replacing mark laid AFTER all darkening: its grey-white bricks (Sheet M18 0.57 to 0.75 of the wall and above) stay pale; laid before the darkening they would come out dark brown (check composed_salt_ratio, and the order test in part E).
walls.rust_bleed_note: The review listed rust with the darkening marks; its tone table (first pass) is a replacing colour, so it is laid with the replacing marks, after the streaks it hangs under

stage_names.6: puddles (WET-ROAD), on top, outside this target

ground.floor_basis: 0.28 of the clean surface albedo (dry). The review proposed 0.35; the sheet's own brown stain is 0.236 wet = 0.295 dry (M20), so 0.35 would clamp the sheet's measured mark (D12). Only crack cores, gum and oil-dot cores may go below it.

wet_dry_rule.rule: The Hook sheet is a WET street (RULINGS 3 October: 'the wet street dark, glistening'), so every ratio measured on it (M18 the foot, M19 the patch, M20 the stains, M22 the head and lower wall, M25 the pipe) is a wet-state ratio. The photographs are dry. A tone row's albedo_mult_linear is the DRY value: dry = sheet ratio / the kind's wet multiplier; the wet look is dry x wet multiplier, applied once (the first pass used sheet ratios as dry and then darkened them again). Dry sources give dry rows directly (M21 soot, M16/M17 streaks, M24 channel). Weather: the game's usual weather is drizzle and rain, never sun (RULINGS 5 October).

looked_at_not_used_note: Downloaded as 2k diffuse maps during the survey of Poly Haven's brick, plaster, concrete and pavement scans; none was measured and no number, colour or shape in this target comes from them. They are listed so the S1 author list is complete and a reader does not look for a measurement that does not exist.

M01.label: Dry asphalt albedo on eight scans
M01.method: Central 70 % of each 2k diffuse map; per-channel median; L* from sRGB D65.
M01.error: +/-3 sRGB levels (JPEG, unknown colour cast of each scan); scans are de-lit albedo.
M01.reading: Worn dry asphalt spans L* 25 to 59; the per-channel median of the three mid scans (asphalt_02 87/86/80, aerial_asphalt_01 97/92/97, asphalt_01 89/80/70) is 89/86/80, L* 37 (the first pass used their mean, 91/86/82).

M02.label: Wear marks on a 30 m x 30 m worn road scan (aerial_asphalt_01)
M02.method: L* smoothed 44 mm (removes the aggregate), minus L* smoothed 0.88 m; dark marks = deficit beyond a threshold; connected components; linear = aspect > 6 and length > 0.5 m; cross-profile averaged about the skeleton of the 16 linear marks.
M02.error: Thresholds +/-1 L*: share 4.6 % (dL 4) to 23.5 % (dL 1.5). Widths +/-15 mm (7 mm pixel). The tile is a tileable processed scan: spacing of features is the photographer's tile, not a street.
M02.reading: Real road wear is low contrast and broad: 4 to 12 % of the area is marked, blobs about 0.22 m, tyre scuffs about 90 mm wide and 2 to 8 m long, with soft edges about 70 mm.

M03.label: Cracks in a worn asphalt scan (asphalt_02, 3 m x 3 m)
M03.method: First pass: counted by eye on the 1400 px montage with a 3.0 m scale: one sealed crack the full 3.0 m, six hairlines 0.2 to 1.8 m, total about 7.3 m. Second pass (the review re-measured it and was right): on the full 2k map (1.46 mm/px, 3.0 m across) the sealed crack lies at x about 250; per row (every second row, 1015 rows), the width of the run below 0.7 of the surface median luminance around the darkest smoothed (2 px) pixel in columns 60 to 420.
M03.error: Length +/-30 % (by eye); width +/-3 mm (1.46 mm pixel, 2 px smoothing); the patch was chosen by its photographer as a cracked road, so it is the worst case. Threshold 0.5 to 0.8 of the surface gives p50 23 to 40 mm.
M03.reading: A cracked road carries 0.8 m of crack per m2; typical road 0.1 to 0.4 (Judgement). The sealed main crack is 15 / 35 / 59 mm wide (p10 / p50 / p90), not 40 to 90 mm, and its core is 0.23 of the surface (L* 13 to 16 on 36).

M04.label: Oil drip speckle on asphalt in a London residential street (urban_street_03, 8k panorama, ground ortho-rectified)
M04.method: Panorama re-projected to a top-down ortho tile at 3 mm/px with camera height 1.6 m; scale proved by the yellow kerb line: 24 to 26 px = 72 to 78 mm (line is 75 mm). Dots = pixels darker than 0.85, 0.75, 0.65 of a 25 px median; components of 4 px or more.
M04.error: Height 1.6 +/-0.1 m gives +/-6 % on areas and +/-6 % on lengths; dot sizes +/-2 mm (3 mm pixel); threshold changes density by a factor 2.5 (167 to 67 per m2).

values.note_region: per_m2_* are over the whole 1.33 m2 region of the view, which includes clean asphalt around the dotted band; in_band_* divide by the band's own area (length x width, central 90 % of the dots)

M04.reading: A parked car's drip band: about 0.3 m x 1.8 m (at least), dots 17 mm, 0.7 of the road's luminance, 154 per m2 inside the band at the darker threshold (379 at the lighter).

M05.label: Utility reinstatement in asphalt (urban_street_02, ortho tile)
M05.method: Ortho tile 3 mm/px, h 1.6 m: rectangle spans 370 x 360 px; seam a dark line 10 to 17 px wide; grass tufts at 3 corners. Second pass (the review re-measured it): luminance profiles across the left seam (mean of 210 rows), seam core against the road's median in a 350 x 600 px open patch; seam colour by 5 px; infill median of x 170 to 330, y 560 to 780; the damp fringe in three boxes.
M05.error: +/-0.1 m on size (height), +/-10 mm on seam; luminance ratios +/-0.05 (JPEG, 8 bit, the line is 3 to 5 px wide).
M05.reading: A cover reinstatement is about 1.0 x 1.1 m with a dark seam of 30 to 50 mm that reads 0.63 to 0.77 of the road (not 0.5), brown-shifted (125/113/100 on 139/127/123); the infill is 0.92 to 0.93 of the road; a damp fringe of 0.80 to 0.86 runs along three edges.

M06.label: Litter along the kerb and on the road (urban_street_02, rectilinear view yaw -165, pitch -20)
M06.method: Pieces counted by eye on a marked picture (automatic bright-blob detection also hit aggregate glints and was rejected): kerb strip about 22 pieces over 5 m of kerb, band 0.3 m deep; road 10 pieces over 13.6 m2. Detected bright bits (aggregate included) had size 7.6, 11.2, 27.7 mm at p10/50/90. Second pass: the same kerb strip (x 150 to 1100, y 225 to 320 of the view) re-segmented by luminance against a 31 px median and colour; each bit classed tan when R - B > 45 on its mean colour.
M06.error: +/-35 % on counts; 8k pixel at 7 m is 5 mm.

values.note_tan: 4 of 13 bits are clearly tan (R - B > 45), 6 of 13 with the borderline ones; the reviewer counted 9 of 24 (0.38) and a tan median 177/140/110 on his exposure; the view's exposure is brighter, the ratios R:G:B agree (1 : 0.79 : 0.62)

M06.reading: The kerb gathers about 4 pieces per metre; open road about 0.7 per m2 (a scruffier estate road; a 1990 shop street would be at or above this). About 4 in 10 filter tips are tan cork-pattern (0.31 to 0.46), the rest white.

M07.label: Patched flags (urban_street_03, ortho tile of the footway, camera-to-footway 1.48 m)
M07.method: Six slab samples by rectangle, mean linear luminance and sRGB; dark slabs 0.20 to 0.24, pale 0.34 to 0.42 (same light); shares and cracks by eye over about 18 slabs.
M07.error: Luminance ratio +/-0.08; shares +/-10 points; slab size +/-15 % (height of the footway).
M07.reading: A 1990-style patched footway has a 0.58 luminance ratio between old and replacement flags and about 1 flag in 9 cracked. The same ortho shows a rough in-situ concrete strip at the kerbside (161/153/149 in the view, texture std 14 against about 5 on the flags): M07b, the basis of footway_infill.

preview_boxes.format: [x0, x1, y0, y1] in preview pixels

M08.label: Flaking paint (peeling_painted_wall, 1.8 m, 0.88 mm/px)
M08.method: Lab k-means (k=2, five seeds) on 512 px, nearest-centroid on 1024 px; minority cluster = loss; components of 3 px or more; edge width = 0.8 x contrast / median boundary gradient.
M08.error: Share +/-2 points; sizes +/-1 mm (1.76 mm px at 1024); edge width limited by one pixel (0.4 mm means 'hard edge').
M08.reading: Flakes are small (17 mm), many (38 per m2), aspect about 3, with hard edges.

M09.label: Craquelure in old paint/render (preconcrete_wall_001, 4 m; cracked_concrete_wall, 1 m)
M09.method: Dark-line detection (L below 10 px local mean by 6 to 8 L*), elongated components >= 40 mm, Zhang-Suen skeleton length; cell size and flake size by eye on the montage.
M09.error: Length +/-30 % (blur merges and splits); width includes blur (true hairline 3 to 8 mm).
M09.reading: Map cracking runs 4 to 6 m per m2 of affected render in cells 0.14 to 0.23 m.

M10.label: Large paint/render loss (rebar_reinforced_concrete, 2 m)
M10.method: As M08, k=3; exposed clusters 0 and 2.
M10.reading: A neglected painted wall can lose up to 40 % of its paint in patches 0.1 to 0.3 m with edges about 10 mm soft.

M11.label: Render loss revealing brick (damaged_plaster, 1.85 m)
M11.method: As M08, k=3; exposed brick = cluster 1.
M11.reading: Render loss: 18 % of the area, patches 67 mm median, up to 0.45 m, edges 11 mm.

M12.label: Damp and mould blotches on painted render (concrete_wall_003, 3 m)
M12.method: As M08, k=3; cluster 2 = dark blotch, clusters 0+2 = yellow stain and blotch.
M12.reading: Damp blotches: 12 % of the wall, median 42 mm, p90 171 mm, 19 mm soft edge; cream render goes to 144/124/97 (x0.45 on Y).

M13.label: Dark corrosion streaks (rusty_painted_metal, 2.2 m)
M13.method: As M08, k=3, cluster 1 = dark streaks.
M13.error: +/-4 points; metal not masonry: geometry only.
M13.reading: Run-off streaks: 24 mm wide (p50), aspect 4 to 12, edges 16 mm.

M14.label: Rust trickle from a fixing and rust drops (asbestos_sheet_02, 1.8 m)
M14.method: Rust = (R - B) > 45 and R > 90 on a crop; trickle rows and widths read from the mask; also by eye.
M14.reading: A rust trickle is 5 to 20 mm wide and at least 0.5 m long, with drops 30 to 90 mm at its end.

M15.label: Moss in joints and the algae gradient at a plastered wall foot
M15.method: As M08 for moss (green cluster); for plaster_brick_01 the row profile of green excess (G - mean(R,B)) and L*, rows 1024 to 2048 are the plaster (lower 1.35 m).

values.tags: Poly Haven's record (api.polyhaven.com/info/plaster_brick_01, read 8 October): tags plaster, rough, old, moss, sewer, tunnel, trimsheet; categories brick, plaster-concrete, wall, man made, dirty, outdoor

M15.reading: Moss fills 12 to 17 % of a wet brick wall as joint lines (mossy_brick and brick_moss_001: physical, a wall). The plaster_brick_01 gradient (the lowest 0.45 m olive-green and 20 L* darker) is NOT a pavement wall foot: Poly Haven tags it 'sewer', 'tunnel' and 'trimsheet', so its green band is a waterline in a trim sheet; the target uses it only as a waterline's colour (Judgement) and no longer cites it as agreeing with the splash profile.

M16.label: Drip streaks hanging from a horizontal joint (concrete_layers, 1.55 m, 0.757 mm/px)
M16.method: L* minus its 12 px mean < -1.5 / -2.5; vertical opening (3 x 1); components with height >= 4 x width and >= 60 mm.
M16.error: Counts +/-40 % (stronger streaks only; by eye 10 to 15 per metre); widths +/-2 mm.
M16.reading: Individual rivulets are 10 to 20 mm wide, 0.09 to 0.45 m long, 8 to 15 per metre of joint, both dark and lime-pale.

M17.label: Streak under a sill bracket on yellow stock brick (urban_street_03, yaw 105, bay window)
M17.method: Scale from brick courses (75 mm gauge, 30 px at 2x crop); column under the central bracket 40 px wide, 180 px long; mean luminance of the column against flanks 0.97; darkest bricks 0.80 to 0.90. Re-measured by the review: course 24 px = 3.1 mm/px, core 60 to 90 mm wide at 0.66 to 0.91 of the flanks (median about 0.8), visible for about 0.30 m.
M17.reading: On a maintained 2019 London stock-brick wall the sill-bracket streak is faint and short: 0.06 to 0.10 m wide, 0.30 to 0.45 m long, 3 to 20 % darker at the core (0.66 to 0.91 at the darkest bricks). The Hook sheet shows no streaks (enlarged 2 to 4 times), so nothing about streak length or density is taken from it; length follows this photograph and M16, darkness is nudged darker by Judgement (D6, section 7).

M18.label: Hook sheet, left gable foot (mood bar, not a photograph)
M18.method: Column-median luminance profile of columns 15 to 170, rows 380 to 730; brick course from autocorrelation (11 px = 75 mm, so 6.8 mm/px); wall reference rows 430 to 600.
M18.error: +/-1 course (75 mm); tone +/-0.05. The sheet is a WET street (RULINGS 3 October): these are wet-state ratios; dry = ratio / the wet multiplier (section 4).
M18.reading: The sheet's foot: 0.33 m black band (0.12 to 0.30 of the wall), a 0.15 to 0.22 m grey-white band on its upper flank (0.26 to 0.46 m), a ragged top stepping by courses.

M19.label: Hook sheet, pale patch on the left gable
M19.method: Patch size from courses: 3.8 courses high, about 1.3 brick lengths wide; colour mean of its core.
M19.error: +/-30 %. Wet-state colours (the sheet is wet): the target's dry patch colour is derived from them once (render_patch).
M19.reading: A buff mortar patch 0.3 m square, 34 L* lighter than the wall.

M20.label: Hook sheet, right pavement stains and road blots
M20.method: Colour of one brown stain 85/60/44 against flag 136/129/131; sizes relative to a 0.6 m flag by eye.
M20.error: +/-30 % size; 5 per 10 m2 by counting 7 stains over about 14 m2.
M20.reading: The mood bar's pavement carries brown stains 27 L* darker than the flags, 0.15 to 0.45 m, about 5 per 10 m2. Luminance ratio of the stain to the flag 0.236 (Y 0.053 against 0.226): a wet-state ratio; dry = 0.236 / 0.80 = 0.30.

M21.label: Soot-blackened stock-brick garden wall beside a cleaner panel (urban_street_03, rectilinear view yaw -125)
M21.method: Rectilinear view 34 degrees wide; scale from the brick courses (22 px = 75 mm, 3.4 mm/px). Sooted panel = box x 20 to 520, y 590 to 720; cleaner panel = box x 590 to 1090, y 590 to 720 (500 x 130 px each, below the coping, same light); median sRGB and L* of each, mean linear luminance of each, HSV saturation of the median colours; row profile in 20 px bands (relative to each panel's mean); a second pair of boxes shifted 10 px and a reviewer's pair gave 0.37 to 0.48.
M21.error: Luminance ratio +/-0.05 (box choice; JPEG); band profile +/-0.05; scale +/-1 course.

saturation_ratio.note: re-made on the same boxes in the third pass (sooted median 89/80/73, C* 6.0 per median and 5.6 per pixel; cleaner 146/129/110, C* 13.1 and 12.8); the second review found 0.68, 0.73, 0.54 and 0.43; the first pass's 0.84 was one HSV calculation on two JPEG median colours and is not what the photograph shows on any per-pixel measure

preview_boxes.format: [x0, x1, y0, y1] in preview pixels

M21.reading: Soot is real and facade-wide on this 2019 street: the sooted panel is 0.377 of the cleaner one in luminance (0.37 to 0.48 by two measurers), nearly neutral per channel (0.37 / 0.37 / 0.43 in linear light), CIE chroma 0.43 to 0.46 and HSV saturation 0.65 to 0.73 of the cleaner panel's (soot is a nearly neutral deposit; the first pass's 0.84 was wrong, D9); under the coping a band about 0.4 m deep is a further x 0.77 to 0.80 on the sooted panel only.

M22.label: Hook sheet: the dark head under the left gable's verge, and the lower wall of the right-hand cottage (mood bar, not a photograph)
M22.method: Head: column medians of columns 15 to 170 in 20 px row bands from the verge down (rows 10 to 230), linear luminance relative to the body (rows 250 to 600); HSV saturation of the median colours; scale 6.8 mm/px from the 75 mm course (11 px). Lower wall: right-hand cottage, columns 1490 to 1590, body rows 380 to 430 against rows 436 to 500 and 516 to 572 in 8 px bands; the course there is about 17 px (4.4 mm/px).
M22.error: +/-0.05 in luminance ratio; +/-1 course in height; the sheet is a generated picture and wet (RULINGS 3 October).
M22.reading: The sheet's walls grime through the brick body, not through streaks: a dark, desaturated head under the verge (x 0.50 to 0.62 over the top 0.2 to 0.75 m, 0.75 to 0.80 at 0.9 to 1.0 m, 1.0 by 1.4 m, saturation 0.65 of the body's) and, on the right-hand cottage, a lower wall about 0.90 of the wall above (0.84 to 0.93, 0.17 to 0.77 m up) with a darker foot. All wet-state values.

M23.label: Rain streaks under sills on a maintained 2019 stock-brick terrace (urban_street_03, five rectilinear views)
M23.method: Five views 40 degrees wide (yaw 30, 60, 90, 105, 120; pitch 14; the yaw-105 view is M17's). (1) By eye at full size: sill and ledge lower edges (painted stone sills, brackets, heads and cornices) with brick below, and whether a streak is clearly visible under each. (2) A column test on every white sill edge that has 0.4 m of brick below it (13 edges in four views): scale from the brick courses under the edge (75 mm), the darkest 80 mm wide column 80 to 380 mm below the edge over the median column of the same edge. The preview holds the yaw-60 view (4 of the 13 edges).
M23.error: Counts by eye +/-3; column ratio +/-0.03 (brick texture std 0.02 to 0.09); scale +/-30 % (course autocorrelation, 2.3 to 6.8 mm/px).
M23.reading: On this maintained street almost no sill carries a visible streak: 1 of about 30 edges by eye (M17), 2 of 13 with a column darker than 0.90, none darker than 0.85. That is 3 to 15 % of sills and 0 to 15 % darkness. It is the cleanest end of the range (S2), so the target keeps the length (M16, M17) and raises the share to 15 to 60 % (typical 35 %) and the darkness to x 0.70 by Judgement (D6); the review's 50 to 70 % has no source.

M24.label: Channel setts and the strip beside them against the open road (urban_street_03, rectilinear view yaw -80, pitch -25)
M24.method: Median linear luminance of boxes in the preview: channel setts x 250 to 550, y 372 to 388; the asphalt strip beside the channel x 250 to 750, y 432 to 470 (the first 0.1 to 0.6 m off the kerb); the open road x 100 to 800, y 560 to 760; row profiles in 5 px bands. The review measured 0.236 for the setts against 0.161 to 0.170 for the asphalt.
M24.error: +/-0.1 in the ratio (the setts are narrow and sloped; JPEG); same exposure for all boxes.

preview_boxes.format: [x0, x1, y0, y1] in preview pixels

M24.reading: The channel is LIGHTER than the road, 1.35 to 1.7 x (the scene says it is 'in the kerb's own concrete rather than asphalt'), and the asphalt 0 to 0.6 m off the kerb is 0.91 to 0.97 of the open road. On the wet Hook sheet the strip between the inner yellow line and the kerb reads about 0.7 of the road (D7).

M25.label: Paint loss and rust on the Hook sheet's gable downpipe; the gully grate of urban_street_03
M25.method: Sheet: the pipe is columns 204 to 210 (about 48 mm wide at 6.8 mm/px; the pipe is 68 mm round), rows 100 to 720; ochre pixels = R > 95, R - B > 35, G > 70, R > 1.3 B; share of rows with ochre, patch heights by connected rows, median colour; the review's measure (columns 199 to 203) gave 7 %. Photograph: the grate in the oil-speckle ortho tile (x 235 to 395, y 160 to 280): pixels with R > B + 18, R > G + 8, luminance 30 to 120; slots black.
M25.error: Share +/-2 points (a 7 px wide pipe, JPEG); patch sizes +/-7 mm (one pixel).
M25.reading: The sheet's downpipe carries paint loss over 5 to 7 % of its length in patches of 20 to 160 mm, pale ochre (125 to 141 / 86 to 102 / 64 to 72) on near-black paint, at the shoe, a collar and a joint. The photographed gully grate is dull red-brown (R - B only 22) with black slots, not bright rust.

M26.label: The worn yellow line (urban_street_03, ortho tile, camera 1.6 m)
M26.method: The line's centre fitted by a quadratic through the yellow pixels (R - B > 45, R > 110); for each column the yellow pixels over the nominal 75 mm strip (25 px along the normal); loss = 1 - mean coverage; gaps = runs of columns with coverage under 0.6; colour of the pixels 5 px inside the yellow mask.
M26.error: +/-8 points on the loss (the edge pixels blend with the road); gap lengths +/-6 mm.
M26.reading: About 22 % (14 to 30) of a street yellow line is lost in chips and gaps (most about 15 mm, one 0.5 m), its edge ragged, its colour a faded, dirt-filmed cream-yellow (about 181/162/120 as albedo, against the scene's fresh 199/168/46).

M27.label: Weathered concrete paving flag albedo (concrete_pavement_02)
M27.method: Central 70 % of the 2k diffuse map: per-channel median, luminance percentiles, L* of the median luminance.
M27.error: +/-3 sRGB levels; a scan, de-lit albedo.
M27.reading: A weathered flag is 134/122/110, L* 52: the same luminance as M07's dark class (133/130/130, L* 54) in a warmer hue; the target takes the scan's hue for the albedo.

M28.label: Hook sheet: Mickey's front under its eaves gutter, and the right-hand cottage's gable under its verge (mood bar, not a photograph)
M28.method: Mickey's front: columns 385 to 445, 10-row bands from row 160 (under the eaves gutter) to row 340, linear luminance relative to the same columns' body (rows 200 to 330); the second review's metres are 10 rows = about 0.07 m. The right-hand cottage's gable: columns 1560 to 1595, rows 322 to 478 in 16-row bands, linear luminance. The second review measured both first; the writer repeated them in the third pass.
M28.error: +/-0.1 in the ratio per band (window frames, the dentil course); the sheet is generated and wet.
M28.reading: Under its eaves gutter Mickey's front has no dark head: 0.64 of the body in the first 10 rows (the dentil course's shadow), then 0.85 to 1.18 (mean 1.0, the review 1.00 to 1.10). The right-hand cottage's gable is flat under its verge. So the head band of M22 belongs to a gable verge with no gutter (the left gable), not to every roof edge (R2).

M29.label: Hook sheet: the brightness of each house between its windows (mood bar, not a photograph)
M29.method: Linear luminance between the windows, rows 190 to 400, by house, as the second review measured it (the writer did not repeat it: the review's boxes were not given). Relative to Mickey's mean 0.081.
